newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assemblyman calls for more regulatory reforms.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assemblyman calls for more regulatory reforms.

text.p: The New York State Assembly Majority Leader on Monday submitted a bill that he said aimed to reform state regulations, easing the burdens for individuals, companies, farmers and other entities.
"We intend to change attitudes throughout the state's regulatory system and stimulate all sectors of the economy," said Michael Bragman, D-Cicero, in prepared comments.
Bragman and the bill's co-sponsor, Joan Christensen, D-Syracuse, said that Gov George Pataki's efforts to reform regulations had produced mixed results.
While some paperwork streamlined and outmoded rules had been abolished "Few significant regulatory changes have been completed and the state's overall regulatory approach has not been altered."
The lawmakers said their "Regulatory Bill of Rights" would:
--guarantee that everyone subject to a state regulation would know its purpose and that the rules clearly explained how to comply with them.
--set a protocol to ensure agencies dealt fairly with the public.
--provide safeguards against arbitrary or unreasonable regulatory actions by the state.
--open the entire regulatory process to oversight by the legislature and review by the public.
